text:
Google acquired the cloud-security firm Wiz to close a security gap with its major competitors, AWS and Azure. This strategic move was driven by Google Cloud under Thomas Kurian, which viewed cloud-security consolidation as the next battleground in the "cloud wars" and bet on AI-driven cloud adoption as a key demand driver [Source: ev-1].

The deal signaled that securing robust cloud infrastructure is now a critical competitive priority for hyperscalers. By agreeing to pay approximately $32 billion in an all-cash deal—the largest acquisition in Google's history—announced on March 18, 2025, Google demonstrated the high value placed on this capability. The transaction also highlighted intense market competition; it followed Wiz’s rejection of an earlier $23 billion offer from Google in July 2024 [Source: ev-1]. Although announced in March 2025 and involving Wiz co-founder Assaf Rappaport as a named principal, the deal completed its regulatory and shareholder steps later that year, with completion reported in July 2025 [Source: ev-1].
